newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH CHESS PRODIGY BECOMES YOUNGEST GRANDMASTER.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH CHESS PRODIGY BECOMES YOUNGEST GRANDMASTER.

text.p: A French teenager became the world's youngest-ever chess Grandmaster on Saturday at the age of 14 years and two months by winning a tournament near Paris.
Etienne Bacrot, who began playing at the age of four, won the masters tournament at Enghien-les-Bains to win the title of Grandmaster after a string of international successes.
Born on January 22, 1983, he beat the previous youth record held by Hungarian Peter Leko who secured the title of Grandmaster at fourteen years six months in 1994.
